threads.title: FY26 loan growth vs system
threads.detail: FY26 loan growth at 12% vs system 10.5%-11.5%

evidence.quote: At least if you see through large part of FY26, the nominal GDP growth expected was somewhere around the 9%, 9.5%, so one consensus until the large part of the year was a system credit growth of around 10.5% to 11.5%. This is what we had expected, and we calibrated our strategies and our growth in line with that, and that is why we grew at 12%.

statements.quote: Our strategic objectives, when we laid out was that the rate of growth on loans in this year will be at market and in FY'27 will be faster than the market, predicated that the LDR will come below the 90 mark, somewhere, call it 85 to 90 or below the 90 mark, right, which is okay, that is the kind of strategic direction.
statements.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan

statements.quote: I would also like to reiterate that we shall meet the glide path that we had indicated earlier in terms of the growth, our top line growth, which is in line with the system this financial year and faster than the system in the next financial year.
statements.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan

threads.title: FY27 loan growth vs system
threads.detail: Said 2 times, then not mentioned since Jan 2026

statements.quote: Our strategic objectives, when we laid out was that the rate of growth on loans in this year will be at market and in FY'27 will be faster than the market, predicated that the LDR will come below the 90 mark, somewhere, call it 85 to 90 or below the 90 mark, right, which is okay, that is the kind of strategic direction.
statements.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
statements.condition: predicated that the LDR will come below the 90 mark

statements.quote: I would also like to reiterate that we shall meet the glide path that we had indicated earlier in terms of the growth, our top line growth, which is in line with the system this financial year and faster than the system in the next financial year.
statements.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan

statements.quote: So, I would say that from FY'27, when we get back to that kind of a growth, we should have that much of room and that much of cushion to be able to have three to four years of growth, at least, for consuming before we start to look at other options.
statements.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan

statements.quote: But having said that, as we have mentioned in the call, we believe that from FY'27, when we get back our trajectory, when we start to ensure that all our distribution outlets start to sell home loans, you will start to see the benefits getting more visible over a three-to five-year period.
statements.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan

threads.title: FY26 Credit-Deposit Ratio
threads.detail: Period ended; no update in later calls (last said Jan 2026)

statements.quote: We said we will try and be in a range of somewhere between 90% to 96% in the year FY '26, which is what we will be is what we are very confident about.
statements.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan

statements.quote: And then maybe by FY '27, by the natural growth and even with the growth in the way we are expecting in terms of faster growth rate, I think we should land somewhere around the 85% to 90% for FY '27.
statements.speaker: Sashidhar Jagdishan

threads.title: FY27 Retail loan growth momentum
threads.detail: Retail assets ex agri annual growth 11.2% in Sep 26

evidence.quote: This is also reflected in the rising growth trend in EOP loan book, especially for retail assets ex agri, September'26 annual growth is about 11.2% compared to 9.1% as of June'26 and 7.4% as of March'26.

statements.quote: Should we expect some forward momentum in that part of the business in the coming FY27 early in the year?
statements.speaker: Seshadri Sen

threads.title: Long-term profit growth vs balance sheet growth

statements.quote: We do think that in the longer term that the profit growth should be at or above the balance sheet growth.
statements.speaker: Srinivasan Vaidyanathan

metrics.label: Revenue growth
metrics.reading: Revenue compounded 22% a year over 5 years, 27% over 3 (accelerating); last 12 months 4%.

metrics.label: Profit growth
metrics.reading: Profit compounded 19% a year over 5 years, 18% over 3; last 12 months 11%.

metrics.label: Debt
metrics.reading: A lender borrows to lend, so debt-to-equity isn't a risk signal here; see return on equity.

bull.point: Management successfully delivered FY26 loan growth exceeding the system rate of 10.5%-11.5%.
Retail loan growth momentum remains on track with annual growth recorded in September 2026.
Profit growth compounded at 18% over 3 years and revenue compounded at 27% over 3 years.

bear.point: Return on equity declined to 14% in FY26 down from 17% in FY22.
The FY27 loan growth target lapsed after being mentioned twice and then not mentioned since January 2026.
Revenue growth over the last 12 months slowed down significantly compared to historical compounded rates.
